The SVG below places all 11 parts once each, with the frame unrotated and the whole assembly shifted by (275, 120) to fit the canvas. I derived the joint positions by reading coordinates from the path data, so the grader's 4–8 px tolerances are not verified by rendering.

The least certain placements are the bottom bracket (inferred from where the seat tube and down tube lines meet, nudged to match the chain length), the fork rotation (chosen so both hubs sit at the same height), and the saddle's collar edge.

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1376 768">
<g transform="translate(275 120)">
<use href="#kit-frame" transform="translate(0 0)"/>
<use href="#kit-rear_wheel" transform="translate(-219.5 107)"/>
<use href="#kit-cassette" transform="translate(-13.6 312.9)"/>
<use href="#kit-chain" transform="translate(38.8 365.3) rotate(6.6) translate(-12.99 -135.31)"/>
<use href="#kit-chainring" transform="translate(268.3 340.05)"/>
<use href="#kit-crank" transform="translate(330.25 404.8)"/>
<use href="#kit-pedal" transform="translate(350.34 543.44) rotate(-107) translate(-21.76 -35.17)"/>
<use href="#kit-fork" transform="translate(663 111.25) rotate(-22.27) translate(-27.62 -5.91)"/>
<use href="#kit-front_wheel" transform="translate(527.05 107)"/>
<use href="#kit-handlebar" transform="translate(631.75 11.75) rotate(-29) translate(-19 -57.8)"/>
<use href="#kit-saddle" transform="translate(245.75 55) rotate(24.6) translate(-172.95 -152.3)"/>
</g>
</svg>
